chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from one of our companions, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace bequeathed from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'What a good mosque is the Mosque of Kufa; a thousand Prophets and a thousand Successors have prayed in it. From it burst forth the oven (of Noah), and therein was built the ship. Its right side is the Pleasure of Allah, and its middle is a garden from the gardens of Paradise, and its left side is Makr.'

So I said to Abu Baseer: 'What does he mean by his word 'Makr'?' He said: 'He means the houses of the Sultan (ruling authority). And the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) would stand at the door of the mosque, then he would shoot his arrow, and it would fall in the place of the date-sellers, so he would say: 'That is from the mosque (part of its area).'
And he (peace be upon him) would say: 'There has been reduced from the foundation of the mosque the like of what was reduced regarding its four corners.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and historical significance of the Mosque of Kufa according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi underscores the spiritual and historical prestige of the Grand Mosque of Kufa, identifying it as a locus of prophetic continuity where a thousand prophets and Imams prayed, and linking it to Noahic history. The Imam clarifies that 'Makr' refers to the ruler's residence, citing Imam Ali’s practice of marking the boundary with an arrow, while noting the structural diminution of the mosque's foundation and corners, a detail often interpreted by Shia scholars as reflecting the political and physical encroachments on the sacred space over time.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from one of our companions, from Al-Hassan Bin Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I heard him<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The best of the Masjids is Masjid of Al-Kufa.

A thousand Prophetsas have prayed Salāt in it, and a thousand succesorsas, and from it did the oven of Noahas burst out, and therein was the ship of Noahas built. On its right is the Pleasure of Allahazwj, and in its middle is a garden from the Gardens of the Paradise, and its left flanis disliked’.

So I said to Abu Baseer, ‘What did he<sup>asws</sup> mean by his<sup>asws</sup> word: ‘Disliked’?’ He said, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> meant the house of the Sultan (ruling authority), and Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> had stood at the door of the Masjid, then he<sup>asws</sup> shot with his<sup>asws</sup> arrow, and it fell in a place of the date-sellers. So he<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘That is from the Masjid (part of its area) ’.
And he<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘And there has been reduced from the foundation of the Masjid the like of what was reduced regarding its four corners’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from certain individuals of our people from al-Hassan ibn Ali from ibn abu Hamzah from abu Basir who have said the following:

“I heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘The Masjid of Kufah is a very good Masjid. One thousand prophets and one thousand executors of the wills of the prophets have performed Salah (prayer) in it. The oven (of Noah) was there wherefrom water gushed forth and the Ark was carved there-from. Its right side houses the matters of the pleasure of Allah, its center houses a garden of the gardens of paradise and its left side lodges evil planners.’

I (the narrator) asked abu Basir, ‘What is meant by evil-planning?’ He replied, ‘It is a reference to the houses of the sultans (kings). ’Amir al- Mu’minin, would stand at the door of the Masjid then throw an arrow, which would reach the places of the sellers of dates and then say, “That is part of the Masjid.”
He would also say, “What is reduced from the basis of the Masjid is like what is reduced from its square.’””
